newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fujimori visits Japan, first time since Lima siege.
newsitem.headline: Fujimori visits Japan, first time since Lima siege.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori arrived in Japan on Wednesday, his first visit to the country since the end of the hostage siege at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima in April.
Fujimori had no official agenda for his first day here, which coincided with Japan's worst ever oil spill, in Tokyo Bay.
On Thursday, Fujimori will hold talks with Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and meet Japanese Emperor Akihito at the Imperial Palace.
In May, Hashimoto visited Peru to thank Fujimori for bringing the hostage incident to an end on April 22 with a raid by Peruvian troops on the diplomatic compound.
Rebels of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement seized the Japanese envoy's house during a reception on December 17, taking several hundred people hostage.

Of the 72 hostages remaining in the diplomatic compound at the time of the raid, 71 were rescued. One hostage and the 14 guerrillas were all killed. Fujimori will also hold a series of talks with leaders of Japanese business circles while in Tokyo. Peru was the top recipient of Japan's yen loans among Central and South American countries in the fiscal year 1995.

The six-day visit is his eighth to Japan since assuming the presidency in 1990. Fujimori, the son of Japanese immigrants to Peru, will also make a tour of Japan's main northern island of Hokkaido on Saturday and Sunday to view agricultural facilities.
